Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Former President Barack Obama joined Democratic candidates in Georgia
Wednesday to rally voters ahead of midterm election day next week.
From member station WABE in Atlanta, Dora Maya Vance has more.
Thousands filled the stands of the arena at Southlake in Marrow, Georgia,
about 25 minutes south of Atlanta.
Attendees cheered on candidates, including Keisha Lance Bottoms,
who's trying to make history as the first black woman elected governor.
However, the crowd erupted when former president Obama took the stage and
called out the Trump administration.
This is what I mean when I say these are not serious people.
They don't have solutions to actual problems.
Just keep throwing distractions out there and hope that you won't notice
that your bills are higher and your life is tougher.
This voter rally is one of many in Georgia this month.
President Trump has made two trips in the past two weeks and it's possible
he'll visit again before the election.
For NPR News, I'm Dora Maya Vance in Marrow, Georgia.
While Obama rallied voters in Georgia,
President Trump made his third trip to Ohio Wednesday.
If you could get out to vote, we're going to have a tremendous victory.
Early voting is underway.
It ends this Sunday, November 1st.
And I'm asking you to pretend that I'm in the ballot.
Speaking in Chillicothe, Trump was on his latest stop in a near daily campaign blitz.
He accused Obama of letting the White House fall into disrepair and he called
for the prosecution of Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola.
Peltola is dismissing a New York Times report saying her campaign had nothing
to do with recruiting a candidate with the same name as Republican
incumbent Dan Sullivan and a bid to confuse voters.
Faculty at Cornell University, one step closer to voting on a no confidence
measure against school leadership, the move comes as Cornell students
and alumni have criticized the school over how it handled sexual
assault allegations from a former student.
Chung Yun Han and Member Station WSKG reports calls for a no confidence
vote have been mounting at Cornell after a former student known as Jane Doe
claimed she was gang raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
While some faculty attempted to delay the vote against Cornell's president,
that effort failed during a heated and divisive meeting on Wednesday.
Mike Thompson, a professor at the university, called the no confidence
resolution, quote, meaningless.
Thompson and other suggested faculty wait until an independent
investigation provides new information.
But proponents of the measure say it signals solidarity with
sexual assault survivors.
Faculty at Cornell will have one week to vote on the resolution.
For NPR News, I'm Jung Yun Han in Ithaca.
The Milwaukee Brewers celebrating their first world series title.
The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays four games to four to one Wednesday
night to win the best of seven.
This is NPR.
In Israel, the vast majority of votes have been counted in Tuesday's
election, but there is still a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin
Netanyahu and his main challengers.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports.
The map could still shift as the rest of the votes are counted, but Netanyahu
and his allies so far have won 53 parliamentary seats.
The center right opposition block is trailing behind Netanyahu with
just 48 parliamentary seats.
Neither side has the 61 seat majority they'd need.
The main question is if the center right opposition will break campaign
promises and agree to partner with Arab-led parties.
Arab parties so far have won a record 19 seats in parliament, thanks to
historically high Arab voter turnout.
Netanyahu is claiming Arab parties, quote, stole the elections, but
it's not published evidence.
It's an apparent attempt to prevent the opposition from partnering with
Arab parties to unseat him.
Next week, Israel's president will decide who to appoint to try to form a
governing coalition.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro says he is the
country's true leader and that he will lead the opposition from the United
States. A flight carrying Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami.
He fled Brazil after refusing to concede the election to President Luis
Anacia Lula da Silva.
Bolsonaro was under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court, accused of
corruption, money laundering and tax evasion.
He denies the allegations.
I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.
